channel.title: Mohammad Efazati: writing
channel.description: Platform engineering, Kubernetes, observability, CI/CD and technical hiring with AI.

item.title: Hiring engineers when AI is in the room
item.description: Banning AI from technical interviews tests a job that no longer exists. What I look for instead, after thousands of interviews, and why the process is the signal now.

item.title: How I build with AI coding agents every day
item.description: A DevOps engineer's working notes on using Claude Code and agent tooling for real infrastructure work: what to hand over, what to keep, and the guardrails that matter.

item.title: The first 30 days with an unfamiliar infrastructure
item.description: How I approach a platform I did not build: map it before touching it, find what actually pages people, and earn the right to change things with small wins.

item.title: Broken on purpose: designing interview challenges that feel like the job
item.description: How we build EasyEnv challenges as Ansible recipes that break a real machine in a believable way, and what makes a good one.

item.title: Kubernetes at the edge, on x86 and ARM
item.description: Lessons from running a 100+ node Kubernetes cluster that spanned cloud servers, NVIDIA Jetsons and Raspberry Pis: multi-arch images, flaky links and installs as code.

item.title: OpenTelemetry before the vendor
item.description: Why I instrument with OpenTelemetry first and pick a backend second, from building an internal developer platform inside a large bank.

item.title: One CI/CD for 200 projects
item.description: Unifying build and deploy across 200+ projects at a payments company: a single SCM strategy, a Jenkins nobody has to worry about, and caching the outside world.
